name: Victoria-Jungfrau Grand Hotel & Spa
positioning: Grand hotel in Interlaken that unites two nineteenth-century hotels, set between Lakes Thun and Brienz in the Bernese Oberland, with the 5,500-square-meter Spa Nescens
best_for: Travelers who want an Interlaken base for summer and winter mountain activities and excursions
Guests planning a spa-focused stay with Nescens better-aging programmes

facts.text: Interlaken lies between Lakes Thun and Brienz, at the foot of the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau mountain range.
The hotel is set amid the mountain scenery of the Bernese Oberland.
The property unites two nineteenth-century hotels and offers views of the Alps.
The hotel sits between two lakes and overlooks Interlaken's central green.
Rooms are decorated in Belle Époque style.
Restaurants and bars include Radius by Stefan Beer, La Terrasse Brasserie, Ristorante e Pizzeria Sapori, Victoria Bar & Terrasse and the Spa Bistro.
At the Victoria Bar, guests can have a drink beneath stuccoed ceilings or out on the terrace.
Inside, the spa has a pool, steam baths, relaxation rooms, a gym and treatment rooms.
The spa offers better-aging programmes from Nescens.
Interlaken offers river rafting, bungee jumping, hiking, biking and golfing in summer, and snowboarding, snowshoeing or tobogganing in winter.
Lucerne, Bern and Zermatt are a day trip away.
The concierge gives tips or puts together a tailor-made offer.

highlights.text: The Spa Nescens covers 5,500 square meters.
The Spa Nescens interiors are inspired by a 1940s boudoir.
Mountain scenery is visible from the spa's outdoor brine pool.
Suite categories include a Yash Chopra Suite and a Tower Suite.
Nearby excursions include the Kleine Scheidegg, the Schilthorn with its James Bond Trail, and the Brienzer Rothorn with its steam rack railroad.

considerations.text: The Kleine Scheidegg, the Schilthorn and the Brienzer Rothorn are excursions from Interlaken, not on site.
In the spa, the sauna area has a mixed Finnish sauna and steam bath, while the other facilities are separated for women and men.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing and a formal atmosphere that may not suit all travelers.
